der that he might obtain
twine and pay threshing accounts, etc., on behalf of Indians of the Assiniboine Reserve. He acted in the matter without
the Department's knowledge, but he accounted for the transactions in his Agency cash book, as will be seen from the
attached statement taken from his returns, which statement is supported by receipts herewith transmitted.

When the matter came to the Department's attention, payments totalling $406.46 bad been made by the Agent to the
Bank in refund of loans.

As it was doubtful when the Indians would be able to repay the balance of the money due, the Department informed
Mr. Commissioner Graham, who had been written to in the matter, that the balance of loan should be retired without
delay, and, consequently, a voucher No. 7275, for $511.00 was presented by Mr. Wilson and was, paid by cheque
No. 685 which was drawn against account No. 145.

When issuing instructions for the issue of the cheque, the Department requested Mr. Graham to notify all the Indian
Agents in the Western Provinces that they must not negotiate loans through the Banks or in any other way in future. It
was further stated that if funds are required to finance a project the whole matter should be laid before the Department
with a definite recommendation. Mr. Graham acted upon these instructions.

So far as the Department is aware, loans from Banks have not been obtained by other Indian Agents.


Yours truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

Indian Trust Fund, Assiniboine Agency: Payment of Loss due to Failure of Home Bank


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, August 7, 1924.

SIR, - Among the vouchers for the expenditure during the fiscal year 1923 - 24 on account of the Assiniboine Agency I
find the following: -

R.D. Wilson, Agent, Transfer from personal account of unexpended balance of cheque No. 3, lost owing to the failure
of the Home Bank of Canada - $68.15.

It appears that an advance of $175 was made to the Agent at the beginning of the fiscal year, which was deposited to
his credit in the Home Bank. Cheques were drawn against this account from time to time for various expenses
connected with the agency, and at the time of the failure of the Home Bank, a balance of $68.15 remained at the credit
of the account. This accountable advance cannot be closed in this way, the unexpected balance must remain as arrears
due. by the Agent until such time as the necessary authority for writing it off is obtained.

Some months after the failure of the bank a dividend was paid the depositors of 25 per cent of the balance standing at
their credit at the time of the failure, did the Agent take the necessary steps to obtain his proportion of this dividend.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


EPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, September 3, 1924.

SIR, - Referring to your letter of the 7th August, bearing on transactions which were carried on at the Assiniboine
Agency, in 1923 - 24, with the Home Bank of Canada, I beg to say that, in September, 1923 this, Department informed
the Department of Finance that the amount at credit of the Assiniboine Agency account with the said Bank, when it
suspended payment, was $133.07, the said amount having been placed on deposit in the effect that in the event of the
liquidation of the Bank, claim should be made to the Liquidator for the preference accorded under the Bank Act to
Dominion deposits. It was further stated that in the meantime, it might not be out of the way to advise the Curator Of
the nature of the deposit. Copy of the letter from the, Department of Finance was sent to Mr. Indian Commissioner
W.M. Graham, Regina, and he was requested to submit a statement in detail, showing to whom the funds - $133.07 -
belong. I enclose Mr. Graham's reply together with copy of the statement which he submitted. You will observe he
stated that cheques totalling $46.40 were drawn against the account, but not cashed, and that cheques amounting
respectively to $3.50, $5.00 and $8.05 were cashed by the payees at the Agency Office and held as cash on hand.

You have pointed out that some months after the failure of the bank, a dividend was paid to the depositors of 25 per
cent of the balance standing at their credit when failure occurred, but I regret to say that Mr. Graham reports he did not
communicate with the Finance Department and did not submit a claim to the Liquidator. Under circumstances, I shall
be glad to be advised as to the course which you consider should now be pursued.


Yours truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.

<!-- page 594 -->
Indian Trust Fund, Blackfoot Indians: Payments to Baird Construction Company, Limited, for Erection of
Small Hospital


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, September 24, 1924.

SIR, - On July 10th, 1923, an Order in Council was passed awarding to the Baird Construction Company, Limited, the
contract for the erection of a small hospital on the Blackfoot Indian reserve near Gleichen, Alberta, the amount of the
contract being $22,425, of which $20,000 was, with the consent of the band, to be paid from the Capital funds at the
credit of the Blackfoot Indians.

From the accounts rendered on the completion of the work I find that in addition to being paid the full contract price
the contractor was allowed $13,282.20 for extras. As the amount allowed for extras added approximately 60 per cent to
the.original contract price for the building, it seems to me either that the original specifications were very incomplete
or that extensive alterations were made in the Plans after the contract was entered into. Among the extras, which
appear to have been charged on the basis, of cost plus 10 per cent, I find an amount of $7,196.82 for a power house
and electric systems; as this exceeds $5,000 I consider that according to the provisions of the Public Works Act,
tenders should have been asked for this work unless there was some special reason for proceeding with it without
calling for tenders.

In addition to the documents which I already have in connection with this work I have to ask to be supplied with a
copy of the specifications and also with copies of any authorization to proceed with the extra works which may have
been issued to the contractors by your department.

I notice that although the Order in Council provides that $20,000 of the original contract price may be paid from the
Capital funds of the Blackfoot Indians, the whole cost of the work including the extras, has been charged against the
Interest moneys of the Band. Should not $20,000 of the cost be transferred to the Capital account.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.

SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 24th September last, respecting the construction of a small hospital on the
Blackfoot Reserve, I beg to say in regard to the items, mentioned in the second paragraph thereof that it was more
economical to have the work done in accordance with the arrangements made than to invite tenders from outside, and I
am attaching hereto copies of the memoranda with reference to this matter, also a copy of the specifications asked for.

In regard to the last paragraph of your letter, I beg to say that through inadvertence this expenditure was charged to
Interest Account, but it has been transferred to Capital Account.


Your obedient servant,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Auditor General.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, September 10, 1923.

MEMORANDUM. - IN connection with the new hospital being built on the Blackfoot Indian Reserve, for which the
contract has been awarded to the Baird Construction Co. of Calgary, a septic tank is. required for the sewage dis-

<!-- page 595 -->

<!-- page 596 -->
posal system. No provision was made for same in the original plans and specifications, as the exact location of the
building had not been determined at the time they were prepared.

Our Inspector of Construction was communicated with and asked to furnish the Department with a sketch showing the
location of the proposed septic tank. Plans and specifications were prepared and the estimated cost of carrying out the
work complete would be approximately $1,800. It is proposed to have this work done by the general contractors on a
proven cost plus ten per cent basis, and I would ask your approval of this expenditure.


J.D. MCLEAN, Act. D.S.G.


Honourable CHARLES STEWART, Interior Department.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, September 18, 1923

MEMORANDUM. - In connection with the new hospital building now being erected on the Blackfoot Indian Reserve,
it will be necessary to install a water supply system also an electric generating outfit for the supplying of electric
current to the hospital and also it is proposed to connect up and supply electric current from this plant to the agency
buildings.

Plans and specifications were prepared for this work, and the cost of same will be approximately $6,000. I propose
with your approval, to have the work carried out by the Baird Construction Co. who are the general contractors for the
building, on a proven cost plus ten per cent basis.

In the installing of the electric lighting plant, it is proposed to use a Lister Bruston engine and generator. This is a very
high class equipment and is entirely automatic in operation. With this system, the life of the storage battery, which is a
great item of expense in lighting plants, is considerably lengthened as this plant is fully automatic and as soon as a
certain discharge, rate is reached on the battery, the plant automatically starts up, taking care of the lighting load and
also charging the battery. The pump used for pumping water will be connected to the same engine that is used for
generating electric current.


J.D. MCLEAN, Act. D.S.G.


Hon. CHARLES STEWART, Interior Department.

Indian Trust Fund: Information Requested with regard to Moneys Collected at Regina by Commissioner
W.M. Graham


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, April 9, 1924.

SIR, - In connection with the examination of the revenue of the Indian Trust Fund for the fiscal year 1923 - 24, I have
to request that you furnish me with copies of any statements sent in by Mr. Graham, Indian Commissioner at Regina,
in connection with his monthly remittances to your department of moneys collected by him on account of grazing and
other leases, on account of payments on land sales, or on any other account.

Are official receipts issued by Mr. Graham for the moneys collected by him? If so, copies or counterfoils of these
reports should be sent in by him to your department and transmitted by your department to this office. If no receipts
have been issued in the past Mr. Graham should be supplied with official receipt books, and copies of every receipt
